newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia banks face some derivative risk-S&P.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia banks face some derivative risk-S&P.

text.p: Australia's four major banks carry only modest risks from derivative products, results of a management survey show, the Standard and Poor's rating agency said on Tuesday.

"The major banks in Australia exhibit a moderate risk appetite for derivative products, which are also subject to sufficient and effective management oversight and are supported by adequate control environments," Standard and Poor's said.
Results of the survey are published in the October edition of Standard and Poor's Monthly Bulletin.
The major four banks are Australia & New Zealand Banking Corp Ltd, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, National Australia Bank Ltd and Westpac Banking Corp .

"The Australian major banks have strong market positions in their Australia and New Zealand home markets, diversified business profiles, large customer bases and sizeable capital resources that underpin their ratings in the AA rating range," Standard and Poor's said.
Each of the banks had substantial capital to deal with an unforseen, but "catastrophic" event relating to derivatives, it said.
A common theme among banks was that they did not need to take risks in the derivative markets, a view which comforts investors, Standard and Poor's said.
The agency said it believed that the oversight provided by the banks for derivatives was sufficient and effective.
"Risk controls for derivatives must seek to protect an institution from incumbent market, trading and operational risks," it said.
"Standard and Poor's believes that the major banks are adequate in this regard."
